b.font: 2. What does it mean to be "skeptical" of something?

ul.style: padding-left: 28px; margin-top: 2px; margin-left: 0px; padding-top: 0px; padding-right: 0px; margin-bottom: 11px;

li.font: To be "skeptical" of something is to doubt its alignment with reality, to lack verification of its constraints (ie. asking what would make the claim true or false, and what evidence or logic can distinguish it from its competitors).

ul.li: "I am skeptical that apples taste good" = "I doubt that my tasting of apples will align with how people enjoy their taste"
"I am skeptical of the Earth being round" = "I have not seen enough evidence to constrain the {Earth's shape} to the full definition of {round}"

li.span: "I am skeptical that he is telling the truth" = "I have not seen enough evidence to constrain {his words} with {what I know occurred in reality}"

ul.li: In other words, to be "skeptical" is not to reject a claim simply because unknowns exist, but to say: "I can’t constrain the presented evidence enough to rationally prefer the explanation over its competitors."

ul.style: padding-left: 28px; margin-top: 2px; margin-left: 0px; padding-top: 0px; padding-right: 0px; margin-bottom: 11px;
ul.li: To be "hyperskeptical" of something is to doubt its alignment with reality, regardless of the verification of its constraints (ie. being ambiguous about what would make the claim true or false, and what evidence or logic can distinguish it from its competitors).
"I am skeptical that apples taste good" = "Even if I seem to like the taste of apples, it could be that my taste buds are malfunctioning, I could be dreaming, or my memory could be unreliable"
"I am skeptical of the Earth being round" = "Even if the Earth looks round with my own eyes, it could be a simulation, a conspiracy, or some unknown phenomenon that perfectly mimics roundness"

li.span: "I am skeptical that he is telling the truth" = "Even if his words seems to align with reality, it could be coincidence, or reality itself could be misleading in some unknown way"

ul.li: In other words, to be "hyperskeptical" is not to resolve doubt but to keep it alive by expanding the space of possibilities without adding new evidence - treating the general idea of being wrong as if it were evidence of being wrong.
Constraints are enough (or known) to distinguish the true claim from the false one
"I have enough constraints to treat this as knowledge"
Constraints aren't enough (or known) to distinguish the true claim from the false one
"I don't have enough constraints to treat this as knowledge"
Constraints are never enough (or known) to distinguish the true claim from the false one
"No amount of constraints can ever be enough to treat this as knowledge"

div.div: In other words, "skepticism" preserves a claim's capacity to be "true", while hyperskepticism removes it - introducing the validity of ad hoc doubt.

span.b: What is the epistemological difference between reasonable and unreasonable uncertainty?

div.span: Acceptance of known constraints: while both assess the uncertainty of a claim,
reasonable uncertainty respects the strength of their established constraints, while unreasonable uncertainty ignores them - speculating about the unknown instead of reasoning from evidence.

switch.text: What is the epistemological difference be...

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 310px; height: 1px; padding-top: 208px; margin-left: 509px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

ul.li: Truth: when there is enough evidence and constraints to identify/define something, distinguishing it from falsehood
Skepticism: when there isn't enough evidence or constraints to identify or define something, being unable to distinguish it from falsehood
Hyperskepticism: when there is never enough evidence or constraints to identify or define something, never being able to distinguish it from falsehood
